A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIMG framework and LongMIT dataset. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-strategy experiments, human quality assessments, LongBench fine-tuning results, scaling analyses, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, dataset-quality comparisons, RULER, IFEval, ArenaHard, and exploratory code-generation results.

M1.justification: The core four-component MIMG pipeline and its principal generation prompts remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a limited code-generation extension: an additional prompt transforms merged code question-answer pairs into programming challenges and solutions.

E1.justification: v2 adds RULER evaluation across context lengths from 4K to 128K, short-context instruction-following evaluation on IFEval and ArenaHard, and exploratory code-question generation using torch.nn documentation. The original bilingual corpus domains and eight LongBench tasks remain.

E2.justification: The original LongBench comparators—ChatQA2, LongAlign, LongAlpaca, and NQ—are retained. The new comparisons introduce base-model controls: InterLM-2.5-7B-Enhance in Table 4 and Llama-3-8B-ProLong in Tables 6 and 8. This is a limited extension of the comparator set.

E3.justification: The stated maximum training sequence length changes from 32K in v1 Appendix C.1 to 4K–128K in v2 Appendix E.1. Added protocols include RULER testing at five lengths, strict/loose instruction- and prompt-level IFEval metrics, and a 100-sample backbone-quality assessment. The PDFs do not establish whether the unchanged LongBench results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct removal ablations for all four MIMG components, measuring quality, diversity, and multi-hop content in Table 5. It also adds cross-backbone human assessments, checks for instruction-following degradation, and a code-generation case study. The earlier strategy sweeps, scaling analyses, and reasoning examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 5 explicitly average three independent manual evaluations, and Table 8 reports 95% confidence intervals for ArenaHard. These add statistical reporting absent from v1; they do not establish additional training runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: All 135 numerical cells in v1 Figure 12 match v2 Table 1. Substantial new results appear elsewhere, including RULER averages of 47.56 for the base model and 70.27 with LongMIT at 128K, component-ablation scores, and instruction-following results. ArenaHard reports LongMIT at 6.7, versus 7.2 for the base model and 4.4 for ChatQA2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content, with notation changes such as Score/Class becoming FS/FC. Neither version contains theoretical proofs. The added metric descriptions explain evaluation practices without introducing substantive mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies the preliminary low-multi-hop and poor-quality findings as applying to Qwen2-72B-generated samples. The principal claims about MIMG, LongMIT, improved data quality, and outperforming larger human-annotated datasets remain; the over-85% and 7.54% claims are retained in the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting quality, diversity, and multi-hop content to different downstream capabilities, a hypothesis explaining long-input classification bias, and explanations of component contributions. It also discusses instruction-following preservation and newly acknowledges limitations from small manual samples, random sampling, and difficulty holding generated questions fixed.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset sample/token counts, manual-annotation procedures, and an explanation that the existing 8.5 threshold was selected using a 200-item verification set. It also supplies the code-extension prompt and revises sequence-length reporting. The hardware, optimizer, retrieval recipe, and main generation prompts were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on LLM-based evaluation, agents, and newer reasoning research. Appendix C.1 additionally positions MIMG as encompassing Self-Instruct and LLM-rechecking procedures. The main long-context research positioning and identification of Quest as the closest work remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and much of the main exposition are extensively rewritten and condensed, with standardized component abbreviations. Dataset-construction material moves into the expanded appendices, which are reorganized from A–D into A–G. Limitations, ethical considerations, and additional explanatory sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Pipeline diagrams are revised, several strategy plots are consolidated into multipanel figures, and the main results display becomes Table 1. New tables and a context-length distribution panel are added, while retained case studies are relocated and their captions corrected.

improvement.justification: The component-removal ablations directly address v1's limited evidence for individual components' contributions. Dataset-quality comparisons, RULER testing through 128K, and instruction-following checks substantially strengthen validation of the central claims. Annotation details and explicit limitations improve transparency while the original LongBench results are preserved. The broader training-length description remains insufficiently tied to individual experiments, and the code extension is weakly validated, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
